text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Talks between the government and the opposition broke up over tax modifications included in the 1997 budget, which is under examination in the Lower House. The centre-right Freedom Alliance now threatens to also stop discussions over constitutional reforms (all).
* In an interview, hard left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti says if the government gives up over taxes it will sink (Corriere della Sera).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said the government and the opposition should maintain political dialogue (all).
* A Milan court confirmed an arrest warrant for disgraced socialist leader and former prime minister Bettino Craxi (all).

* As the privatisation of telecom holding Stet seems set to be delayed, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi is said to be ready to sell Finmare, a financial company for sea transport owned by state holding IRI. Ciampi is expected to meet today European Commissioner Karel Van Miert in Brussels to discuss government plans for an IRI capital increase by the end of the year (La Stampa).
* Fiat honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli said there is an "absolute necessity for Italy to join EMU from the start." (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
